decision_description: A conflict exists between two Phase 7 (Tier 4) budget artifacts governing gate_09. The lump-sum budget gate assessment (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json) declares gate_pass_declaration='fail' via blocking inconsistency BLK-01, because no budget response was received in the lump-sum integration channel (docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/). The unit-cost budget derivation (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json) declares gate_pass_declaration='pass' with all four line items (living_allowance, mobility_allowance, research_training_networking, management_and_indirect) resolved to Confirmed, total_eur=220723.5, no unresolved components and no blocking inconsistencies. The governing issue is which budget source applies to gate_09. The instrument recorded in Tier 3 (docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json) is MSCA-PF with budget_regime unit_cost. Under the C1 amendment to CLAUDE.md §8.4 and §8.1, the budget gate is instrument-conditional by source: for unit-cost instruments the sanctioned budget source is the internal deterministic derivation (confirmed_months x published_rates x host_country_coefficient), byte-equal-checked, and the external lump-sum response is not the applicable source. The tier resolution: the Tier 3 instrument type governs over the default lump-sum integration channel, so the unit-cost derivation prevails and gate_09 passes; the lump-sum assessment's 'fail' is inapplicable to this instrument because the lump-sum channel is not the budget source for unit-cost instruments. The categorical Phase 8 block of §8.4 remains satisfied because a complete, structurally consistent, fully Confirmed budget is present.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Treat the lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json 'fail' (BLK-01) as the authoritative gate_09 outcome and keep Phase 8 fully blocked.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: CLAUDE.md §8.4 (C1 amendment) makes the budget-gate source instrument-conditional; for the unit-cost MSCA-PF instrument recorded in Tier 3 selected_call.json, the lump-sum external response is not the sanctioned source, so its absence cannot constitute the applicable blocking gate failure.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Prepare and await an external lump-sum budget response through the integration channel before re-evaluating gate_09.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Lump-sum externalisation applies only to lump-sum instruments (CLAUDE.md §8.1); introducing an external lump-sum response for a unit-cost instrument would substitute a non-sanctioned budget source and contradict the deterministic-derivation anti-fabrication guarantee.

tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.4 and §8.1 (C1 instrument-conditional budget gate amendment): conflict between the Tier 4 lump-sum budget gate assessment (fail) and the Tier 4 unit-cost budget derivation (pass) is resolved by the instrument type recorded in Tier 3 selected_call.json (MSCA-PF, budget_regime unit_cost); for unit-cost instruments the internal deterministic derivation is the sole sanctioned budget source and governs gate_09 over the lump-sum integration channel.
rationale: The two Phase 7 budget artifacts cannot both determine gate_09, and the contradiction must be resolved explicitly rather than by selecting the more convenient source (CLAUDE.md §12.3). The C1 amendment scopes 'exclusively external' budget computation to lump-sum instruments only; for unit-cost MSCA-PF, determinism supplies the anti-fabrication guarantee and the deterministic derivation is the mandated source. Because unit_cost_budget.json resolves every component — including the sole host-dependent line (living_allowance, host_country=HU, coefficient 78.7%) — to Confirmed with no unresolved or blocking items, the §8.4 gate condition is met by the sanctioned source. The lump-sum assessment validated a channel that does not apply to this instrument, so its 'fail' is a false negative for gate_09 and does not weaken the categorical, instrument-independent Phase 8 block, which is satisfied by the present complete and structurally consistent budget.
